🎯 Functional Correctness | 🟠 Major | ⚡ Quick win

🧩 Analysis chain
🌐 Web query:
In Go's net/url package, does ParseRequestURI accept absolute-path values like "/foo" without a scheme/host?
💡 Result:
Yes, Go's net/url.ParseRequestURI accepts absolute-path values, such as "/foo", without a scheme or host [1][2][3]. The function is specifically designed to parse URLs as they might be received in an HTTP request line [1][2]. According to the official documentation, ParseRequestURI interprets the input string as either an absolute URI or an absolute path [1][2]. Because absolute paths are valid request-targets in HTTP, they are accepted by this function [4][3]. It is important to note that ParseRequestURI assumes the input string does not contain a fragment suffix (#fragment), as web browsers typically strip fragments before sending the URL to a server [1][4].
Citations:

1: https://pkg.go.dev/net/url
2: https://pkg.go.dev/net/url@go1.26.4
3: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51069484/url-validation-seems-broken
4: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.26.4/src/net/url/url.go



Reject path-only values here
url.ParseRequestURI accepts inputs like /foo, so these fields can still pass validation without being actual URLs. If IconURL and GotoLocation must be full URLs, require a scheme/host or switch to a stricter URL check.
